title: Phrasal verbs for IELTS
summary: Nhóm cụm động từ học thuật (carry out, phase out) và cụm mô tả xu hướng (level off, bottom out) — dùng đúng tách/không tách.
whyItMatters: Người học hay tránh cụm động từ vì sợ sai, rồi viết toàn *do*, *make*, *increase*. Nhưng một số cụm là chuẩn học thuật (*carry out research*, *phase out coal*, *account for 20%*) và nhóm mô tả xu hướng (*level off*, *bottom out*) là ngôn ngữ bắt buộc của Task 1. Vấn đề không phải dùng nhiều, mà là dùng **đúng loại** và **đúng vị trí tân ngữ**.

sections.heading: Three types, three behaviours
body: **Intransitive** phrasal verbs take no object: *The economy slowed down.* *Sales picked up.* **Inseparable transitive** verbs keep the particle next to the verb: *We must **look into** the complaint* — never *look the complaint into*.

**Separable transitive** verbs allow the object between verb and particle: *carry out the survey* or *carry the survey out*. When the object is a **pronoun**, it must go in the middle: *carry **it** out*, never *carry out it*.
Three-word verbs are always inseparable and always keep their order: *put up with*, *cut back on*, *look forward to*, *get away with*, *come up against*.

sections.heading: Academic phrasal verbs worth using
body: A small set is fully acceptable in formal writing because there is no simpler single-word equivalent in common use: **carry out** (research, a survey, a review), **put forward** (a proposal, an argument), **phase out** (a fuel, a subsidy), **bring about** (change), **account for** (a proportion), **point out** (a limitation).

Others are neutral enough for Task 2: **rule out** (exclude), **look into** (investigate), **set out** (present systematically), **take on** (accept work or responsibility), **break down** (divide into parts, or stop working).

These verbs let you vary your vocabulary without sounding informal. *The study **carried out** in 2022 **points out** that rural clinics **account for** only 12% of spending* is band-8 academic prose built almost entirely from phrasal verbs.

examples.right: The researchers carried out a survey of 2,000 households.
Several economists have put forward a different explanation.
The government intends to phase out coal subsidies by 2030.

sections.heading: Trend phrasal verbs for Task 1
body: Task 1 needs movement verbs, and the phrasal set is compact and precise: **take off** (start rising fast), **pick up** (start rising after a slow period), **level off / flatten out** (stop rising or falling), **bottom out** (reach the lowest point and stop falling), **peak** is a single verb, but **edge up / edge down** describes a small change.
Use them as alternatives to *increase/decrease* when the shape of the line matters: *Sales **bottomed out** in 2012 before **picking up** sharply.* Two phrasal verbs in one sentence, both accurate.
Do not use them for data you have not seen. *Take off* implies a sudden acceleration; if the line rises steadily, *rise steadily* is the honest description.

examples.note: The particle is part of the meaning — *level* alone means *make flat*.

examples.right: Sales bottomed out in 2012, then picked up sharply.
The figure edged up by just 2% over the decade.

sections.heading: Register: when to replace a phrasal verb
body: Many phrasal verbs are informal and have a Latinate single-word equivalent that examiners prefer: *put off → postpone*, *find out → discover*, *go up → rise*, *look at → examine*, *talk about → discuss*, *get rid of → eliminate*, *come up with → devise*, *deal with → address*.
The test is simple: if a one-word verb exists and is common, use it in Writing. If the phrasal verb is the standard term (*carry out research*, *phase out subsidies*), keep it.
In Speaking, the opposite applies — phrasal verbs make you sound natural. So learn both registers and switch deliberately between Task 2 and the speaking test.

sections.heading: Putting phrasal verbs to work in a paragraph
body: A single well-placed phrasal verb can carry a whole policy narrative. Consider: *The city **set out** to cut car use by 30%. It **carried out** a series of pilot schemes, then **phased out** free parking in the centre. Congestion **levelled off** within two years, and cycling **picked up** sharply.*

That paragraph uses five phrasal verbs, all standard, and no repetition of *increase* or *do*. This is what range looks like in practice — not rare words, but the right verb for each stage of the story.
Keep the density controlled: four to six phrasal verbs in a 250-word essay is plenty. More than that starts to sound like a vocabulary list rather than an argument.

examples.right: The council set out to cut emissions by a third.
examples.note: **set out to + verb** = begin with a stated aim.

examples.right: Free parking was phased out over three years.
examples.note: Passive + separable verb; *phased out* stays together in the passive.

examples.right: Cycling picked up sharply once the lanes opened.

commonMistakes.wrong: The researchers carried out it in 2022.
commonMistakes.right: The researchers carried it out in 2022.
commonMistakes.why: Với đại từ tân ngữ, cụm tách được phải đặt đại từ ở **giữa**: `carry it out`, không phải `carry out it`.

commonMistakes.wrong: We are looking forward to hear from you.
commonMistakes.right: We are looking forward to hearing from you.
commonMistakes.why: **look forward to** + V-ing vì *to* ở đây là giới từ, không phải `to + infinitive`.

commonMistakes.wrong: The government cut back spending on health.
commonMistakes.right: The government cut back on spending on health.
commonMistakes.why: Cụm đúng là **cut back on + noun**. Thiếu *on* là lỗi giới từ.
**level off** mới có nghĩa *ngừng tăng/giảm*. *Level* một mình nghĩa *làm phẳng*.

commonMistakes.wrong: The essay sets out that rural schools lack funding.
commonMistakes.right: The essay points out that rural schools lack funding.
commonMistakes.why: **set out** cần `to + verb` khi nói mục đích (*sets out to show*), hoặc + noun (*sets out the argument*). Với mệnh đề *that*, dùng **point out**.

ieltsTips: Trong Task 1, dùng cụm mô tả **hình dạng** đường biểu đồ thay vì chỉ nói tăng/giảm: *bottomed out*, *levelled off*, *picked up*, *edged up*. Bốn cụm này đủ để mô tả hầu hết biểu đồ đường.

Trong Task 2, dùng **carry out** và **put forward** thay cho *do* và *say*: *Several studies **carried out** in low-income countries **put forward** a different explanation.* Câu vừa chính xác vừa đúng register học thuật.

Đừng dùng cụm động từ thân mật trong Writing. Nếu có từ một chữ tương đương (**postpone**, **discover**, **eliminate**), hãy dùng nó. Giữ cụm động từ cho những khái niệm không có từ thay thế tự nhiên.

Học cụm động từ theo **cấu trúc**, không theo nghĩa: ghi *carry out + research/survey*, *phase out + subsidy/fuel*, *account for + %*. Khi biết tân ngữ đi kèm, bạn sẽ không phải ghép từ trong lúc viết.

exercises.question: The team carried ___ a survey of 2,000 households.
The government plans to phase ___ coal subsidies by 2030.
Which sentence is correct?
options: The researchers carried out it last year.
The researchers carried it out last year.
The researchers carried out last year it.
The researchers out carried it last year.
exercises.explanation: A pronoun object goes between verb and particle.

exercises.question: Sales ___ in 2012 and then rose sharply.
I am looking forward to ___ from you.
exercises.explanation: **look forward to + -ing** — *to* is a preposition here.

exercises.question: Agriculture accounts ___ about 40% of total water use.
The committee will look ___ the complaint.
The council cut back ___ spending on consultants.
We cannot put ___ with such high levels of waste.
